newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak IRB head sees credit restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Slovak IRB head sees credit restructuring.

text.p: The first priority of the new management of Slovak Investicna a Rozvojova Banka IRB is to restructure its loan portfolio, its president-designate said on Thursday.

Vojtech Vranay, newly appointed to the bank's board and expected to be formally installed as president next week, said in a statement for the official Slovak news agency TASR that too much should not be read into the changes to the board.
"It is a step which the shareholders took...to achieve a higher standard of quality, making it highly attractive both for clients and shareholders," Vranay said.
IRB said earlier on Thursday that president Jozef Tkac and three other members of the board of directors were replaced at the request of its majority shareholder, Kosice-based steelmaker VSZ a.s..
Vranay said the new management would establish new priorities for the future.
"The first will be the speedy process of revitalising and restructuring the loan portfolio," Vranay said.
The restructuring costs will be borne solely by the shareholders and will not affect the clients, he added.

"On the contrary, the solution of the problem of classified loans will enable the bank to grant credit and services under attractive conditions for the clients." Vranay added. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563 3687
